name: PdfCraft
tagline: A free, open-source PDF reader and organizer that works like Acrobat - view, combine, split and secure PDFs on your own machine.
sentence: Open, search, annotate, combine and split PDFs with the same tools Acrobat has - without paying Adobe $20 a month.

visual.alt: PdfCraft viewing a PrintCraft Showcase PDF: an All Tools sidebar listing Export, Fill and Sign, Edit, Create, Combine, Organize, Comments, Scan and OCR, Protect, Redact, Compress. A comments panel shows 20 annotations and 13 form fields.
visual.caption: The PDF workbench showing the tools sidebar, a document with 20 comments, and 13 fillable form fields.

board.say: You need to read, combine, split or annotate PDFs regularly - but Acrobat costs $20 a month and free viewers can't organize or secure files.
board.eg: You have 5 scanned contracts and need to combine them into one PDF, rearrange the pages, and add a password.

board.say: You open PdfCraft and drop in your PDF files, or point an AI agent at it through its command interface.
board.eg: Open a PDF by double-clicking it, or let Claude Code drive PdfCraft through its built-in command channel.

board.say: Your PDF files - including encrypted ones (RC4 through AES-256) and complex documents with layers, forms and comments.
board.eg: A 200-page report with threaded comments, a fillable tax form, or a set of PDFs to merge.

board.say: It renders, organizes and manipulates PDF files locally, with crash recovery and atomic saves.
steps: View PDFs with tiled rendering for deep zoom, bookmarks, search-as-you-type, and multiple layouts (continuous, single, two-up)
Organize pages: rotate, delete, insert, move, combine files, extract or split by page count
Fill forms, toggle layers, read and add threaded comments, and handle attachments
Save with incremental, atomic writes that keep original bytes intact - with autosave every minute
board.eg: The project's own test: 963 of 983 pdf.js test files open and render cleanly, zero crashes across the corpus.

board.say: Organized, annotated or secured PDF files, saved on your own computer.

outputs.eg: 5 scanned contracts merged into one file, or a 200-page report split into chapters
A tax form filled out and saved, or a contract with your threaded review comments
A PDF with AES-256 encryption and owner-set permissions, ready to share

before: Combining, splitting or securing PDFs means paying Adobe $20 a month for Acrobat - or hunting for a free tool that handles each task separately.
Free PDF viewers show the pages but can't organize, combine, fill forms or add security.
after: One free app for reading, combining, splitting, annotating and securing PDFs - with Acrobat's tool layout.
Autosave and crash recovery protect your work. Incremental saves keep the original bytes intact.
uses_note: PdfCraft is 9 days old and in early alpha. Named real-world use is still very early.

pulse.gain: +5.4K stars in its first 9 days. Part of the ArtCraft suite.

coverage.title: ArtCraft Apps - open-source Rust alternatives to Adobe's creative suite

steps: [Download PdfCraft](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/releases) for your computer (Mac, Windows or Linux) and install it.
Open a PDF and try the [tools](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft#organize): search, rearrange pages, and combine two PDFs into one using Organize > Combine.
Try filling a form if you have a fillable PDF, and check that the comments panel shows threaded annotations.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft

If that scan passes: download and install PdfCraft, open a sample PDF, try the page organizer and combine two files. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No data found for installer size. Builds from source with `cargo run --release -p pdfcraft` (requires Rust 1.90+).
footprint.memory: No data found. Uses tiled rendering for efficient memory use on large documents.
footprint.runs_on: Mac (universal), Windows (x64, arm64, x86), Linux (x86_64, aarch64, needs glibc 2.35+), FreeBSD and the web (via WebAssembly).

best_for: You need one free app that reads, combines, splits, annotates and secures PDFs - instead of paying Adobe $20 a month
You handle encrypted or complex PDFs (forms, layers, threaded comments) and want a viewer that renders them correctly
skip_if: You need to edit PDF text or create PDFs from scratch - PdfCraft is a viewer and organizer, not a full Acrobat editor. Content editing is not built yet.
You need OCR, Office import/export or XFA forms - those features are listed as thin or missing

alternatives.name: SumatraPDF
alternatives.line: A fast, lightweight free PDF viewer on Windows. Very stable but no page organization, form filling or annotation.

alternatives.name: Okular
alternatives.line: KDE's free document viewer. Annotations and form filling, but no page organization or file combining.

watch: **About half of Acrobat Pro's features.** PdfCraft views, organizes and secures, but cannot edit existing text, create new PDFs from scratch, or run OCR. It is a workbench, not a full editor.
**Part of the ArtCraft suite by storytold.** Same maker as PhotoCraft, LightCraft, FilmCraft and ArtCraft. Early alpha, built by one developer with AI.
**Rendering uses an external crate.** Pages are currently rendered by the hayro crate while the project builds its own renderer. Quality may vary on complex layouts.
**Linux needs glibc 2.35 or newer.** That means Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+ or equivalent. Older distributions are unsupported.
